title: Finding global maxima and minima
goal: Find the absolute highest and lowest values of a continuous function on a closed interval $[a, b]$ by testing critical points, sharp corners, and both endpoints.

beforeThis.skill: Don't forget the endpoints! On a closed interval $[a, b]$, the highest or lowest value very often happens right at the left edge $x = a$ or right edge $x = b$.

questions.asking: Sketch the graph of a function defined for all real $x$ that reaches a highest value overall but has no lowest value.
questions.statement:
Sketch a function $f(x)$ such that:

  • $f(x)$ is defined over all real numbers
  • $f(x)$ has a global max but no global min.

questions.asking: Sketch the graph of a function defined for all real $x$ that stays strictly above the $x$-axis yet never attains a highest or lowest value.
questions.statement:
Sketch a function $f(x)$ such that:

  • $f(x)$ is defined over all real numbers
  • $f(x)$ is always positive
  • $f(x)$ has no global max and no global min.

questions.asking: Sketch the graph of a function defined for all real $x$ that attains its lowest overall value at two distinct points, $x = 5$ and $x = -5$.
questions.statement:
Sketch a function $f(x)$ such that:

  • $f(x)$ is defined over all real numbers
  • $f(x)$ has a global minimum at $x = 5$
  • $f(x)$ has a global minimum at $x = -5$, too.

questions.asking: Find the global maximum value and global minimum value of $f(x) = x^2 + 6x - 10$ on $[-5, 5]$ and where they occur.
questions.statement: $f(x) = x^2 + 6x - 10$. Find all global extrema on the interval $[-5, 5]$.

questions.asking: Find the global maximum value and global minimum value of $f(x) = \frac{2}{3}x^3 - 2x^2 - 30x + 7$ on $[-4, 0]$ and where they occur.
questions.statement: $f(x) = \dfrac{2}{3}x^3 - 2x^2 - 30x + 7$. Find all global extrema on the interval $[-4, 0]$.
